title: Reduce dashboard query tail latency via windowed prefetch + tombstone aggregation
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Some dashboard list and exploration queries exhibit long tail p95/p99 latencies when scanning across many small shards or when encountering high tombstone density (deleted/soft-deleted rows) during range reads. This is particularly visible for admin tenants and large customers. Existing mitigations (basic LRU microcache, hedged reads) help median latency but don't sufficiently reduce the tail for large cursors.

Proposal: Implement an experimental server-side feature that combines: (1) windowed probabilistic prefetch hints — lightweight per-tenant hinting to prewarm likely-next-page index blocks using a compact bloom-derived hint set; (2) tombstone aggregation/consolidation during index scans — detect dense tombstone spans and consolidate them into a short-circuit path that avoids per-row processing; and (3) projection-aware index reads to reduce payload work for paginated queries. The feature will be behind a feature-flagged canary rollout with observable metrics and automatic rollback.

Goals: reduce dashboard query p99 latency by at least 25-40% for affected query shapes without increasing median latency or significantly raising per-request CPU. Maintain correctness (no missing rows) under MVCC semantics.

Notes: This ticket focuses on engine + API-layer changes for the dashboard query API; client-side SDKs are unaffected. The approach trades minimal staleness risk (short window prefetch might return slightly earlier snapshots) for latency, but we will preserve MVCC read consistency for canonical read paths and only allow relaxed hints for non-final exploratory queries as configured by route labels.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for sample tenant query shape reduced by >=25% on canary cluster compared to baseline (metric: dashboard.query.latency.p99.route=list)
no increased error rate or data correctness issues across 24h canary run
feature can be toggled per-tenant and per-route via runtime flag
end-to-end automated test coverage for tombstone consolidation behavior and projection-aware reads
rollout & rollback playbook documented and validated with SRE runbook runbook-linked
steps: Design spec: finalize windowing heuristic, bloom hint encoding, and tombstone detection thresholds (doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/EXP-WindowedPrefetch)
Implement compact hint encoding in query planner and hint store in tenant-metadata service
Add prefetch worker in read pipeline with low-priority thread pool and bounded concurrency
Implement tombstone aggregation: detect contiguous delete markers across index leafs and short-circuit scanning with an aggregated cost estimate
Add projection-aware index read path to skip materializing unused columns for paginated endpoints
Bench locally (unit tests + microbench harness) then run canary on staging cluster -> measure p50/p95/p99
Ship feature-flag, enable for 2% of production traffic, monitor for 24h, expand to 20% then 100% if green
Postmortem & performance regression dashboard added to console (query latency breakdown by phase: index-read/prefetch/deserialize)
decisions: Use probabilistic bloom-based hint encoding to keep metadata size per-tenant <1KB and avoid hot metadata store blowup
Prefetch will be async and best-effort: failures do not affect correctness path; requests can fall back to canonical scan
Tombstone consolidation will run under a sampled path initially (10% of scans) to compare behavior before enabling globally
We will preserve MVCC strong reads for 'export' and 'audit' routes; hints only apply to interactive list/explore routes where slight snapshot skew is acceptable
Use incremental rollout with automatic disable if p99 increases or error rate crosses threshold (alert thresholds: +10% errors or +15% p99)
No schema changes to storage; consolidation is read-path only to avoid migration window complexity
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Design review complete. Lina Park (PM) and Ravi Menon (SRE) approved telemetry matrix. Trade-off note: bloom false positives may cause some wasted prefetch but acceptable given cache TTL is short.
2025-02-24: Implemented hint encoder and hint-store shims. Bench harness shows prefetch reduces index-read wall time by ~28% in synthetic wide-scan workload.
2025-02-28: Tombstone aggregator prototype merged behind flag. Unit tests added for edge cases (interleaved deletes, MVCC visibility).

2025-03-02: Canary rollout started at 2% on prod-read cluster us-west-2. Initial 6h telemetry: p50 unchanged, p95 down 12%, p99 down 22% for list-route-A. No increase in 5xx or data-correctness alerts.
2025-03-05: Can expand to 20% after SRE thumbs-up if next 24h remains stable. Preparing performance dashboard slices and rollback automation (k8s flag toggler).
dependencies: ENG-521400 (kv-cache: expose eviction metrics to telemetry)
